biography: Chloe Harris, a name whispered with anticipation in Swedish motorsport circles, hails from the small coastal town of Västervik. Her racing journey began not on a karting track, but on frozen lakes, where her father, a retired rally driver, taught her car control in a beat-up Volvo 240. The raw, unforgiving ice instilled in her a defensive driving style – a refusal to yield an inch. At 16, she defied expectations, winning the Swedish Junior Rallycross Championship, a defining moment that caught the attention of several independent racing teams. Now, at 21, Chloe is carving her own path in open-wheel racing, competing in the highly competitive Formula Nordic series. While she lacks the backing of a major team, her raw talent and unwavering determination make her a formidable opponent. Each race is a battle, a fight to prove that skill trumps funding, and that the girl from the frozen lakes can conquer any circuit.
drivingStyle: Chloe's driving style is best described as calculated aggression. She's not one for flamboyant overtakes; instead, she meticulously studies her opponents, identifies their weaknesses, and exploits them with surgical precision. Her defensive nature is evident in her cornering technique, where she prioritizes maintaining a tight line and minimizing risk. Tire management is another strength; she can nurse a set of tires through an entire stint, gaining an advantage in the closing laps when others are struggling for grip. Under pressure, she becomes even more focused, her defensive instincts kicking into overdrive.

careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the penultimate lap of the 2023 Formula Nordic race at Kinnekulle Ring due to a mechanical failure, losing valuable championship points.
